details.publicNotes:
At first glance, volt rams look like sheep. However, the branching scorch marks on their horns and their particularly fluffy wool are the first signs of the electric charge that dances across their bodies. Those who approach closer find their skin tingling and their hair standing on end.

The unique structure of a volt ram's wool allows them to generate and store static electricity with their movements and use it in various ways. As the charge grows, the volt ram's wool gathers into pointed spikes. These spikes are a sure sign that the electric charge has grown to dangerous levels. While a volt ram's fleece is dangerous if improperly handled, it is a valuable crafting component for magic items.

Beings with a natural resistance to electricity prize volt rams as livestock in order to harvest their fleece. Even those without such protections occasionally accept the risks inherent in keeping a flock. Reports from these eccentric shepherds state that volt rams are relatively easy to care for, all things considered, as the creatures' lighting is more than enough to scare off any would-be predators. A tool for safely releasing the ram's stored charge is an essential part of these shepherd's toolkits.

In the wild, volt rams travel in large flocks. They sometimes choose to accompany runebranded aurochs (Battlezoo Bestiary, page 79). Runebranded aurochs that live among volt rams often develop enhanced powers over electricity.

Both male and female volt rams have horns. Male volt rams are more direct and aggressive with potential threats to the flock, while female volt rams are more likely to store their charge as a threat display. Juvenile volt rams, sometimes called spark lambs, gradually develop their ability to hold a charge over their first year of life. Newborn lambs can't generate more than an unpleasant tingling sensation.

Spring Showers

In springtime, when young volt rams battle each other for dominance, wise shepherds know to wear their sturdiest rain gear. When a pair of volt rams charges each other, the impact of their horns produces a crash of thunder that can be heard for miles. These battles are usually accompanied by a violent, if short-lived, cloudburst.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 5/12/22 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning, piercing), perception item, skill items (Acrobatics, Athletics, Survival)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, constitution, electricity, energy resistant (electricity, vitality), sensory (darkvision), strength, wild, wisdom

description.value:
Trigger A creature hits the volt ram with a melee attack roll using either an unarmed attack or a metal weapon

Requirements The volt ram has Stored Charge

Effect Some of the electricity stored in the volt ram's fleece surges into the target, dealing @Damage[1d6[electricity]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:18|basic] save).

A volt ram's wool is exceptionally capable of storing electricity. Whenever a volt ram is targeted by or in the area of an effect that deals electricity damage, or when it uses Running Charge, its wool captures and stores the electric charge.

The volt ram releases stored static electricity in a blast of crackling lightning. All creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] around the volt ram take @Damage[2d6[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:16|basic] save). A creature that critically fails the saving throw is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}. The volt ram can't use Discharge again until it Stores Charge.
The volt ram runs and charges up the static electricity as it does. It Strides twice and Stores Charge.
